# PART 2 — CONFLICTING OR AMBIGUOUS AUTHORITIES

- **Non-tiered waiver approval authority varies significantly across publications with no unified routing standard.** Different AFIs assign non-tiered waiver approval to different offices: the requestor's commander (AFI 36-1301, AFI 36-2113, DAFI 31-126), the AFGM OPR (AFGM 2026-36-2033), the CMSAF (AFI 36-2109), AFPC/DPM (AFI 36-2122), AFPC/DP3AM (AFI 36-2135), AFPC/DPPSP with AF/A1P concurrence (AFI 36-2406), the publication OPR (AFI 36-2129), or HQ AF/A4S/CFM (DAFI 31-118). This creates a fractured landscape where non-tiered waiver routing depends entirely on which AFI governs, with no overarching directive clarifying the hierarchy. — See AFGM 2026-36-2033 vs AFI 36-1301 vs AFI 36-2109 vs AFI 36-2113 vs AFI 36-2122 vs AFI 36-2129 vs AFI 36-2135 vs AFI 36-2406 vs DAFI 31-118 vs DAFI 31-126.

- **Ambiguous "approval authority" for 8F000 SDI requests (AFI 36-2113 §§2.1.14–2.1.15).** The statements reference an entity that "serves as the approval authority" for RegAF requests to serve beyond four years in the 8F000 SDI and for members serving in another SDI, but the extracted text does not identify WHICH role or office holds this authority. The subject of these paragraphs is defined elsewhere in the document and is not present in the extracted statements. — See AFI 36-2113 §2.1.14 and §2.1.15.

- **Overlapping authority for position and tenure waivers for key leadership positions.** The SAE has explicit approval authority for PEO/Deputy PEO/ACAT I–II PM position and tenure waivers, while "the appropriate senior level official within the command" approves these for "all other key leadership positions." The boundary between SAE-controlled and command-controlled positions could be ambiguous for positions not explicitly enumerated (e.g., ACAT III PMs or positions with dual reporting chains). — See AFI 36-1301 (multiple sections on position waivers, tenure waivers, and selection authority).

- **Over-grade approval during rotation has an unclear approval chain.** AFI 36-2113 §6.4.7 states the over-grade requires "a recommendation by the CCM, approval authority, WG/CC or equivalent," but it is ambiguous whether these are three separate sequential approvers, whether the "approval authority" and "WG/CC" are the same entity, or whether the comma-separated list represents alternatives. — See AFI 36-2113 §6.4.7.

- **Evaluation exception authority overlap between CSAF and HAF Deputy Chief of Staff, Personnel.** AFI 36-2406 states "only the CSAF may approve exceptions" but then immediately grants the HAF DCS/Personnel "similar authority" for general officer management cases. The extent to which this authority is co-equal or subordinate to the CSAF's is not clearly delineated. — See AFI 36-2406 (general exceptions).

- **Meeting minutes/decision sheet approval appears assigned to two different chairs.** DAFI 31-118 assigns meeting minutes/decision sheet approval to both an unnamed chair (§3.3.5.2.2.2, marked "ADDED") and the SFEC chair. It is unclear whether these refer to the same entity or represent two different bodies with the same procedural authority. — See DAFI 31-118 §3.3.5.2.2.2 vs SFEC chair provisions.

- **Wing Commander escalation authority (AFI 36-2406) vs. general "approval authority" finality.** AFI 36-2406 states that if the "approval authority" recommends disapproval, the request goes to the WG/CC for final decision. Separately, the same AFI states "the decision of the approval authority is the final decision … and may not be appealed" (in the context of criminal conviction comment waivers). These two provisions create confusion about when an approval authority's decision is truly final versus when it can be escalated. — See AFI 36-2406 (disapproval escalation vs. criminal conviction waiver finality).

# PART 3 — AUTHORITY GAPS

- **No identified authority for selecting or approving CMSAF, CCM, or Group SEL positions.** AFI 36-2109 states it "establishes the selection and approval authority" for these positions, but the extracted statements do not identify which specific role or body holds selection/approval authority. The actual assignment of authority is not present in the extracted corpus.

- **No identified authority for approving religious accommodation denials.** AFGM 2026-36-2033 states the AF will approve pre-accession religious accommodation requests unless they adversely affect military necessity, but does not specify who makes the determination that military necessity is adversely affected or who has the authority to deny such requests.

- **No clear authority assigned for determining "extreme circumstances" for late changes to evaluation records before central selection boards.** Both AFPC MLR Office and ARPC/PB may approve late changes on a "case-by-case basis" in "extreme circumstances," but no criteria or authority is defined for what constitutes "extreme circumstances" or who makes that threshold determination.

- **No authority identified for the 55-pound personal effects limit for EPWs.** AFJI 31-304 references that certain items are not part of the 55 pounds of personal effects each EPW is authorized to take, but no authority is identified for granting exceptions to or adjudicating disputes about this limit.
